source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Banana bunches are ready for harvest roughly 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on variety and growing conditions, and harvest timing is judged by visual ripeness cues rather than a fixed calendar date - the guide describes waiting until the fruit's ridges (angles) have rounded out and filled in, typically corresponding to about 75-80% physiological maturity, rather than waiting for the fruit to yellow on the plant.

To harvest, the whole bunch is cut down with the stem, generally supported by a second worker so the bunch does not fall and bruise; farmers are advised to pad the cut bunch (for example wrapping it in banana leaves) during transport to avoid bruising the fruit, since bruised fruit ripens unevenly and loses market value.
